topic: n8n 2.0 AI Agent Tool Node: Complete Tutorial (2026)

competitors.title: Build an AI Agent with n8n — Step-by-Step Guide (2026)
key_points: AI Agent node introduced in n8n 1.19.0 (August 2024) enables autonomous agents that reason, select tools, call external APIs, and loop until task complete
Uses ReAct (Reasoning and Acting) framework internally: Thought → Action (tool call) → Observation → repeat until Final Answer
Three complete agent examples: Web Research Agent (SerpAPI + HTTP Request), Customer Support Agent with Postgres Memory, Spreadsheet Data Processing Agent
Covers both OpenAI GPT-4o and Ollama local models as LLM backends
Memory node types: Simple Memory (RAM), Postgres Chat Memory (persistent), Redis Chat Memory (high-traffic)
Contabo VPS self-hosting option from €4.50/month with pre-installed n8n
Max Iterations setting: default 10, recommend 15-20 for complex tasks

competitors.title: n8n AI Agents Tutorial: Build Smart Workflows Step by Step
key_points: n8n is open-source workflow automation with native LangChain integration — agents, tools, memory, models as visual nodes
AI Agent uses hierarchical structure: Trigger → AI Agent → Chat Model + Tools + Memory → Output
Tools Agent uses ReAct loop and works with any tool — covers 90% of use cases
Specialized agents: SQL Agent (database queries), Plan and Execute Agent (sub-steps), Conversational Agent (simple chat), OpenAI Functions Agent (OpenAI-native, faster)
MCP Client Tool connects agents to external MCP servers, auto-discovers tools
Agent-to-agent workflows via Call n8n Workflow tool (manager delegates to workers)
Production deployment: Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis, queue mode for horizontal scaling, reverse proxy with SSL
n8n supports OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, Cohere, HuggingFace, Ollama models
Self-hosted Community Edition free; n8n Cloud starts at $20/month (2,500 executions)

competitors.title: Building AI Agent Workflows in n8n: The 2026 Complete Guide
key_points: AI agents handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously — n8n's native AI Agent node makes this accessible without code
Traditional workflows: trigger → process → output; AI agents: goal + tools → self-directed execution
Cost optimization: set Max Iterations limits, use Window Buffer Memory for short sessions, cache LLM responses

Use cases: customer support (ticket categorization, routing, draft responses), content research (multi-source search + structured briefs), data normalization (varying formats/missing fields), anomaly monitoring
System prompt is the single most important factor for agent behavior — defines personality, constraints, and output format
Semantic memory for long-running agents: vector-based search over conversation history
